regions.name: Aravali Ranges
regions.notes: Stony ranges. Site of Mask Family schism, Jharwa massacre, and hidden sanctuary of Vara-Ma/Orek/Thren.

regions.name: Ganges Lava Sea
regions.notes: One of the most extreme magmatic zones in the setting: active volcanic rifts that cool and solidify into vast jagged black basalt plains and lava fields. Extreme zone where magma meets ocean. Deep-sea vent lineages were pushed to the surface here and evolved obsidian carapaces that withstand direct magma exposure; extremophile gastropods fuse basalt and metallic ore into armoured shells along the lake shores. The fauna are heavily armoured and heat-resistant, often fused with volcanic minerals. The bestiary groups the magmatic and glacial extremes together, with underworld portals at the far end. Species here default to rare.

regions.name: Gedrosian Desert
regions.notes: Arid interior, and young: the harbour, the fossil channel and the caravan road all date the water's departure to within cultural memory rather than to geological time. Forty authored species, all desert-placeable.

regions.name: Narmada Plateau
regions.notes: Volcanic highlands. Site of academic culture in later eras and source of Narmada Man blessing.

regions.name: Saraswati Delta
regions.notes: Primary setting of Civilization Dawn / Lothal Era. Home to Harappan settlers and Kia clan.

regions.name: Shattered Sea & Mappa Mundi
regions.notes: Marine and island belt east of the delta, grouped in the bestiary with the deep rainforests of Mappa Mundi. The Cognitavi claim the volatile sea and build their own bird-fortresses here, holding integrated nests on the coral docks of Tamralinga Port; Tuli seafarers of the Vanga Maritime League work the pearl routes under Cognitavi guidance. The Mappa Mundi rainforests are the refuge of the displaced Silvanus and Sylvian lineages after the Vanara cataclysm.

regions.name: Tethys Sky Routes & Floating Islands
regions.notes: Sky-oases above the Tethys Sea. The islands are held up by lodestone cores of hyper-magnetised, Permian-irradiated ore that repels the Earth's field into localised anti-gravity bubbles, a legacy of the shattering of Gondwana; warped gravity on the undersides sends rainwater overflowing upward as inverted waterfalls. Home to the bark-skinned Vyom-Yakshis, the Cognitavi Cloud-Hermits and their monasteries, and traded by orca-blimp mariners.
regions.biomes_note: Deliberately empty. Sky species have no equivalent among the ten ground biomes, so everything filed here is held as lore and never placed on a tile.

field_maps.name: The Dry Harbour
field_maps.arrival: The harbour wall runs for four hundred paces and the mooring rings are still in it, at the height a loaded hull would sit. There is no water. There has been no water for long enough that the nearest is two days' walk, and short enough that the rings have not rusted through.
field_maps.notes: Fourth field map, and the one about time rather than about knowing. Everything here was built or evolved for a wetter world that ended inside cultural memory, and nothing about it is mysterious -- it is all simply out of date. First map where canon's own species populate the ground: forty Gedrosian species, all placeable.

field_maps.name: Dwarka
field_maps.arrival: Half of Dwarka is under water and the half that is not has been rebuilt twice on top of itself. Nobody here treats the sea as an enemy or the gate as a wonder. Both are simply conditions, like weather, and the whole city is arranged around living beside them.
field_maps.notes: Third field map. The one where the method is tested: local knowledge is not merely useful here, it is right, and the academy's three tidy explanations are all wrong. Gives `crosses_at` a consumer without making the crossing species placeable -- you find what they left, never the animal.

field_maps.name: Lothal
field_maps.arrival: The delta takes a long time to become a city. Reeds, then reed-and-mud, then mud with brick in it, and then brick cut by someone who expected it to last. The tower is visible from a good way out, or the half of it still standing. Somebody has hung washing across the third storey.
field_maps.notes: Opening field map. Lothal after the Great Shattering: the Harappan city is a half-buried relic and survivors are camped inside it rather than beside it, so the same ground is a settlement and a ruin at once. Kept small and legible -- this is where the player learns how to look.

field_maps.name: The Narmada Plateau
field_maps.arrival: The road up the scarp is the only part of the plateau anyone built. Everything above it was already here: black rock in steps a hundred feet high, holding a flat green country the sea never reached. They will tell you at the top that this is why the University is here. They are right, and it is not the whole reason.
field_maps.notes: Second field map, and the counterweight to Lothal. At Lothal local knowledge was right and the academy was quoted from a distance; here the academy is a room the player stands in. The Long Archive is not foolish -- it is rigorous and its record begins at the Shattering, so it has four hundred years of excellent measurements against a baseline that is itself the wound. Large scale, hills and mountains, so the overworld reads as travel rather than as two versions of the same map.

points_of_interest.name: The Stepped Quarry
points_of_interest.description: Cut basalt in courses, and between two of the courses, a bed of something else.
points_of_interest.arrival: They quarried here for the halls and stopped when they hit a seam that would not dress. The seam is nine inches of pale ash between two floods of black rock, and it is full of small dead things lying in the order they died.
points_of_interest.notes: The evolution discovery. A quarry rather than a dig, so the section is exposed by accident and read by the player rather than presented by a scholar.

points_of_interest.name: The Bone Midden
points_of_interest.description: Where the city puts what it cannot eat, cannot burn, and does not want.
points_of_interest.arrival: Every settlement has a midden and this one has the usual fish spine and oyster shell and broken pot. It also has, at intervals, layers of something else — and the intervals are the interesting part.
points_of_interest.notes: Evidence rather than encounter. The crossing species stay `lore` and unplaceable; what the player finds is what they left.

points_of_interest.name: The Caravan Ground
points_of_interest.description: Where the road stops for the night, and has for longer than the road has made sense.
points_of_interest.arrival: The camp is on the wrong side of the ridge for shelter and the wrong distance from the well, and every caravan stops here anyway, because this is where you stop.
points_of_interest.notes: The road is the map's other clock: it still follows a river that is not there.

points_of_interest.name: The Cloud Stair

sub_locations.name: The Lower Flights
sub_locations.description: Cut into the scarp, wide enough for two, worn in the middle like any stair anyone ever used.

sub_locations.name: The Turn
sub_locations.description: Where the stair stops climbing the rock and starts climbing away from it. There is no rock under the last four steps and they are still there.

points_of_interest.description: A stair up the scarp that keeps going after the scarp stops.
points_of_interest.arrival: You can follow it with your eye until the cloud takes it, and the cloud is not always there, and it goes up past where the cloud is. Nobody at the University will say it is not a stair. They will say it has not been surveyed.
points_of_interest.notes: The anomaly, and the hook toward region_tethys_sky_routes for a later map. Deliberately unresolved -- the ladder ends at a good description rather than an explanation, because some things should stay open.

points_of_interest.name: The Customs House

sub_locations.name: The Weighing Floor
sub_locations.description: Sunk a hand below the doorway so a spilled load could be swept back. The sweep marks are still there, going the same way every time.

sub_locations.name: The Strongroom
sub_locations.description: Barrel-vaulted, no window, and the door frame is worn at the height of a shoulder rather than a hand — people came out of it carrying.

points_of_interest.description: A building for taxing cargo that stopped arriving.
points_of_interest.arrival: It is the best-built thing for sixty miles, because it was the building that made money, and it is intact because nobody has had any reason to take it apart.
points_of_interest.notes: Where the archaeology and the linguistics meet. The tariff boards are the map's clock.

points_of_interest.name: The Drowned Dockyard
points_of_interest.description: Straight lines under the water, at what used to be a quayside.
points_of_interest.arrival: The basin was cut square and lined with fired brick, and salt water has been in it long enough that a reef has taken the corners. Fish that have never seen the open sea live in a harbour that no longer reaches it.
points_of_interest.notes: Lothal's dock. An archaeological site being eaten by an ecological one, which is the tone of the whole era.

points_of_interest.name: The Drowned Seawall
points_of_interest.description: Three seawalls, one behind the other, each built when the last stopped working.
points_of_interest.arrival: You can wade the outermost at low water and stand on the innermost without getting your feet wet, and between them is four hundred years of a city agreeing, twice, that the sea had won that round.
points_of_interest.notes: The geography discovery and the sober counterweight to the gate: the thing actually destroying Dwarka is the sea, which nobody finds remarkable either.

points_of_interest.name: The Eastern Field
points_of_interest.description: Good flat ground, well watered, and nothing on it.
points_of_interest.arrival: Eight acres of level silt beside a channel that never runs dry, and not a stem on any of it. The camp plants here every spring out of stubbornness and takes nothing off it. Something came up out of the ground during the Shattering and has not gone back down.
points_of_interest.notes: The solarpunk hook, and what the actionable rung acts on: restorable once the player understands both the poison and the rice.

points_of_interest.name: The Fossil Channel
points_of_interest.description: A river-shaped valley with gravel in it, sorted the way running water sorts gravel.
points_of_interest.arrival: From the ridge it is unmistakably a river and from inside it is a valley with stones in it. The stones are the argument: rounded, graded fine to coarse across the width, and lying exactly as a current would leave them.
points_of_interest.notes: The geography discovery. The sorting is what makes it evidence rather than a shape someone imagined.

points_of_interest.name: The Gate Court

sub_locations.name: The Outer Court
sub_locations.description: Paving, a drain, and a low wall someone maintains. It looks like a yard because it is one.

sub_locations.name: The Threshold
sub_locations.description: Where the air stops being the same on both sides. You can stand with one hand in each and feel the difference at the wrist.

points_of_interest.description: A swept courtyard with a doorway in it that does not lead anywhere in this city.
points_of_interest.arrival: It is swept. That is the first thing, and it undoes most of what you were prepared for: somebody sweeps the gate court, the way somebody sweeps a threshing floor, because things come through and the mess has to go somewhere.
points_of_interest.notes: The anomaly, presented as municipal infrastructure. The horror of it, if there is any, is entirely in how unremarkable the locals find it.

points_of_interest.name: The Glass Scar
points_of_interest.description: A seam of fused sand, running straight, where nothing should have been hot enough.
points_of_interest.arrival: Green-black glass, in a line you could follow at a walk, and under it sand that was never heated at all. Whatever did this did it fast enough that the heat had no time to go downwards.
points_of_interest.notes: The anomaly, and the map's only unexplained thing. Kept small and undramatic: it is a date stamp more than a mystery.

points_of_interest.name: The Herders' Terraces
points_of_interest.description: Stone steps up a hillside, grazed by goats, described in the archive as ornamental.
points_of_interest.arrival: Two hundred steps of dry-laid stone, each one a little lower at the outer edge than the inner. Marn's goats are on them. The University's survey calls them a devotional feature and gives them a paragraph.
points_of_interest.notes: The archaeology discovery and the restore target. A paragraph in the survey against two hundred courses of deliberate engineering is the whole argument of this map in one image.

points_of_interest.name: Kavik's Tower

sub_locations.name: The Lower Courses
sub_locations.description: Twenty-two storeys of red sandstone, of which four remain standing and the rest lie in roughly the order they fell.

sub_locations.name: The Stair Shaft
sub_locations.description: The stair survives because it was cut into the core rather than built against it. It goes up into daylight and down into water.

sub_locations.name: The Flooded Undercroft
sub_locations.description: Below the waterline the sandstone is cold and the carving is sharper, having been spared four hundred years of weather.

points_of_interest.description: Four storeys of red sandstone where the chronicles promise twenty-two.
points_of_interest.arrival: It did not topple. It sat down. The upper courses came straight through the lower ones and the whole thing settled into the delta mud like a foot into silt, which is why four storeys are still square and true and everything above them is a slope of dressed stone.
points_of_interest.notes: Kavik's tower, the landmark settlement_lothal records. Enterable rather than merely visited, and the undercroft gates on knowing the safe channels -- a player who has not done the mangrove work cannot reach the best of it.

points_of_interest.name: The Last Well
points_of_interest.description: The one well still reaching water, and the reason anybody is still here.
points_of_interest.arrival: Forty families, one well, and a rope long enough that two people are needed to work it. Nobody has drilled a second. Teshk will tell you why, and the answer is not money.
points_of_interest.notes: The people. The well is the map's whole economy and its countdown.

points_of_interest.name: The Long Archive

sub_locations.name: The Reading Floor
sub_locations.description: Long tables, north light, and the working copies -- which are copies of copies, and say so on the spine, which is more honest than most places manage.

sub_locations.name: The Sequence Stacks
sub_locations.description: Every measurement the University has taken, in the order it was taken. Four hundred years of rainfall, riverflow, birds arriving and birds leaving. It is beautiful and it is the whole problem.

sub_locations.name: The Unread Shelf
sub_locations.description: What came up the scarp already written and has never been transcribed, because nobody here can read it and nobody will admit that in writing.

points_of_interest.description: Four hundred and eleven years of measurements, kept perfectly.
points_of_interest.arrival: The stacks run back further than the lamps reach. Okhi says there are eleven thousand bound volumes and that she has personally copied four hundred of them, and then, without any change of tone, that she has no idea whether the oldest are true, only that they are old.
points_of_interest.notes: Where the through-line resolves. The sequence stacks gate on discovery_archive_baseline so the player cannot be handed the thesis before earning it; the unread shelf gates on a word, which is the point at which the plateau's own script stops being decoration.

points_of_interest.name: The Camp in the Kilns
points_of_interest.description: Smoke, and washing strung between two courses of Harappan brick.
points_of_interest.arrival: Forty-odd people live in the kiln quarter, because the kilns were built to hold heat and still do. Nobody has repaired anything so much as leaned things against other things until they stopped falling. A child watches you from a doorway that used to be a flue.
points_of_interest.notes: The living settlement, inside the ruin. Deliberately not a quest hub: people here trade leads, tea and old maps. Mixed survivors -- a Mask Family remnant, a Silvershore straggler, delta fishers -- thrown together by the Collapse rather than by kinship.

points_of_interest.name: The Marsh Shrine
points_of_interest.description: Pale mangroves standing in a ring, and something at the centre that is not a tree.
points_of_interest.arrival: The Kia did not build the shrine so much as agree about it. A ring of ghost mangrove, a stone with a hollow worn into the top, and a great deal of water that is shallower than it looks if you know where to put your feet.
points_of_interest.notes: Kia rather than Harappan. Where the channel discovery is learned and the marsh-lurker can be watched.

points_of_interest.name: The Mooring Stones
points_of_interest.description: Four hundred paces of harbour wall, with the rings still in it.
points_of_interest.arrival: You can put your hand through a mooring ring and feel where a rope wore it thin on one side only, which tells you the current ran that way, which tells you there was a current.
points_of_interest.notes: The image the map exists for. Deliberately the first place a player is likely to reach.

points_of_interest.name: The Narmada University
points_of_interest.description: Nine halls around a yard, and every one of them measuring something.
points_of_interest.arrival: It is smaller than the word suggests and busier than the quiet suggests. Nine halls, a yard with a rain gauge in it that has been read twice a day for four hundred and eleven years, and a great many people being careful. Nobody here is a fool. That turns out to matter more than the alternative would have.
points_of_interest.notes: The academy as a place rather than a citation. Deliberately sympathetic -- the scholars are rigorous and generous with the player, which is what makes the structural error land.

points_of_interest.name: The Salt Orchard
points_of_interest.description: Fruit trees dying at one end and something else doing well at the other.
points_of_interest.arrival: The orchard is half orchard. The seaward rows are salt-killed and standing, and through them, in the shade the dead trees still cast, something with the wrong leaf shape is doing extremely well.
points_of_interest.notes: The botany discovery. An establishment event in progress, which is a slower and more frightening thing than a monster.

points_of_interest.name: The Silted Granary
points_of_interest.description: A grid of brick chambers filled to the brim with silt, and something growing out of them.
points_of_interest.arrival: The granary held the city's grain on raised platforms so the flood could not reach it. The flood has since reached it. What is remarkable is not that the chambers filled but that the crop came back on its own, red and thin, growing out of the tops of the walls.
points_of_interest.notes: Where the rice discovery lives. The ruin is already doing the restoring; Varuna only has to notice.

points_of_interest.name: The Tide Market
points_of_interest.description: Trading twice a day, around a tide that decides when the floor is a floor.
points_of_interest.arrival: The market runs on the low water and stops on the high, so the day has two mornings and two evenings and everybody's sense of time is bent around it. Prices are quoted in what the tide will allow rather than in what a thing is worth.
points_of_interest.notes: Where the people are. Deliberately ordinary: the point of Dwarka is that the extraordinary thing is treated as weather.

points_of_interest.name: The Walking Spring
points_of_interest.description: A spring the archive records at a fixed point, and a line of dead stonework saying otherwise.
points_of_interest.arrival: The water comes out of the hillside cold enough to hurt. Forty paces downslope there is a stone basin, dry, well made, and obviously built to catch exactly this. Forty paces further there is another.
points_of_interest.notes: Geography and botany both. The dry basins are the evidence and they are visible on arrival -- the player can see the answer before they can explain it, which is the right order.

points_of_interest.name: The Watch Stair
points_of_interest.description: Steps up the old wall, kept clear, with a good view of the court.
points_of_interest.arrival: Somebody keeps these steps clear of weed, and there is a worn patch at the top where people stand. They are not watching the sea from here.
points_of_interest.notes: The observation post. Exists so the gate can be watched over time rather than visited once, which is what its discovery needs.

npcs.name: Bekh

lines.text: Mask Family, yes. There is no family and there are no masks, so it is mostly a way of saying which brick I sleep under.
We plant the eastern field every spring. My mother did. Her mother did. It is not stubbornness, it is that the ground is good and we cannot see what is wrong with it.
My grandmother walked to the shrine at night and came back dry. I have never known how and I have stopped asking whether it was true.
The niche in the stair. Something stood in it when my grandmother was small. She would not say what.

npcs.notes: Mask Family remnant with no masks and no family, related to character_kavik far enough back that the line means little to her. Would NOT settle -- she is the one who stays, because somebody has to be here when the rest go. The ending is better for her refusing.

npcs.name: Marn

lines.text: The steps? The steps have always been the steps. Good grazing, stays green late. You are the first person to walk up them looking at them.
Khet. Not step -- khet. It means the water is held. I do not know why we call them that, we just do.
We lose one a year to the millet and we have always lost one a year to the millet. If you are telling me that is a choice and not a weather, I will need to sit down.

npcs.notes: Holds two of the map's answers inside ordinary vocabulary and has never had a reason to examine either. The counterpart to Thrali, and pointedly not a wise elder -- he is a working herder with a job on.

npcs.name: Okhi

lines.text: Eleven thousand volumes. I have copied four hundred. I do not know if the oldest are true, only that they are old, and that is not nothing.
There is a shelf I dust and cannot read. Thirty years. If you learn what is on it I would like to be told, and I would like it told to me before it is told to the halls.
No. Somebody stays. You have all found the thing that is wrong with this place and you are all leaving with it, and the eleven thousand volumes are still here and still need copying.

npcs.notes: The one who will not come. Deliberately not a tragedy and not a rebuke -- she is right that somebody has to stay, and the ending should let her be right rather than treating her as a failed recruitment.

npcs.name: Pell

lines.text: I keep the inner wall and I sweep the court. They are the same job to me: something arrives, and it has to go somewhere.
In mist, yes. Not every mist. You will want the stair and three days, and you will be the first person to sit them who was not being paid.
No. My father rebuilt this wall and I have rebuilt it and my son will. You are asking me to leave a job that is not finished, and it is never going to be finished, and that is not a reason.

npcs.notes: The one who will not come, and for the opposite reason to Bekh: not somebody has to stay, but the work does not end and that is not an argument for stopping. Sweeps an interdimensional gate as municipal maintenance.

npcs.name: Ravi

lines.text: My family has kept this building for four generations and there has been nothing to keep it for during any of them. You are the first person to ask what the boards say.
Tolu. It is not a good, it is a draught — the shallow water at the head of a channel. Whatever came in on it, we taxed at nine times salt and I do not know what it was.
The last board is not finished. I have known that since I was a boy and I have never once wondered about it until you stood there wondering out loud.

npcs.notes: Four generations of custody with nothing to be custodian of. Would settle -- the building is a duty, not a home, and he has never been asked to do anything else.

npcs.name: Sura

lines.text: Everything the city cannot use comes to me eventually. Most of it is fish. Some years it is not.
You want the thin layers. My mother showed me where they are, and hers showed her, and none of us has ever been asked about them before today.
The orchard? The orchard is finished. I would rather you told me something about it that I can do than something about it that is true.

npcs.notes: Holds four hundred years of stratigraphy as a family trade and has never been asked. Would settle -- the midden is a living, not a home.

npcs.name: Teshk

lines.text: Three wells were dug before this one and all three are dry. People say we were unlucky in where we put them. We were not unlucky in where. We were unlucky in when.
The rope has been lengthened twice since I was small. I did the second one. I expect to do a third and I do not expect to do a fourth.
No. Forty families work this rope and it takes two. If I go, it takes two of somebody else, and there are not two of somebody else to spare.

npcs.notes: Will not leave, and for a third distinct reason: not duty like Bekh, not unfinished work like Pell, but arithmetic -- the rope needs two people and there are not two to spare.

npcs.name: Thrali

lines.text: You will want the basin at night, after rain. The water goes silver and they come up. Ask me why and I will tell you I do not know.
My grandfather had a word for it. Thal-something. He is dead and I have half of it.
The far banks I cannot work. Water looks the same everywhere out there and it is not the same, and I have a family.

npcs.notes: Delta fisher, Kia by descent, half his grandfather's vocabulary lost. Gives the opening hook and is the first person the player can materially help. Would settle -- he has nothing holding him here but the fishing.

npcs.name: Uma

lines.text: Three kilns, every year, and every year the same three. I have stopped minding. It is something to do in spring.
After the flood? Nobody cuts reed after the flood. -- No, I am listening. Say it again.

npcs.notes: Keeps the camp's roofs on. The smallest possible help, and deliberately the first one available: the player learns that knowing when to cut a reed counts as helping.

npcs.name: Vessa

lines.text: You will want the rain series. Everyone wants the rain series. Read the first ten years of it and then come and tell me what you think we are measuring against.

I have written it three times and withdrawn it three times. Not because they would be angry. Because they would ask what the pre-Shattering figure was, and there isn't one, and that is the end of the conversation.
My grandmother's people counted years by what happened in them. The halls would call that anecdote. It is also the only record that reaches back past the wound.

npcs.notes: The scholar who is already most of the way there and cannot say so in an acceptable form. Would settle -- she has been looking for somewhere the question is allowed.

biomes.name: Sea
biomes.notes: Tethyan water. Not walkable in the game.

biomes.name: Floating Island
biomes.notes: The island surface itself — glowing moss, prismatic glass herbs, aero-mangrove groves at the edges. Held up by lodestone cores of Permian-irradiated ore.

biomes.name: Island Underside
biomes.notes: The inverted world beneath an island, where gravity is warped and rainwater falls upward. Sky coral calcifies here and holds the crumbling rock together; the Asura-tainted gargoyles shelter in it.

biomes.name: Open Sky
biomes.notes: The air between islands, worked by gliders and migrants — aero-mantas, sky-faring orcas, ballooning spiderlings. The orca-blimp routes run through it.

biomes.name: Naraka Rifts
biomes.notes: The rift country beyond the portals: sulphurous rivers, blood-warm pools, the twilight zone. Naraka water is not the Saraswati's, so its creatures do not simply swim into a delta — they cross into this realm at a gate. See `crosses_at` on the species themselves; the Dwarka Gate is the established one (settlement_dwarka, event_shadow_pact, event_naraka_portal). A Naraka creature met in this realm should therefore be met near a gate, not spread through ordinary water.

biomes.name: Lava Sea
biomes.notes: The molten surface and scalding shallows of the Ganges Lava Lake, where magma meets ocean. Distinct from the volcanic highlands around it, which are ordinary mountains and remain renderable.
